content.executive_summary:
- **Tier 1 -- Core LPBF / Laser / Sensing fit (4 faculty)**: Chinedum Okwudire (S2A Lab, LPBF laser path + Ulendo vibration compensation), Kira Barton (Barton Research Group, smart manufacturing + LPBF AM + iterative learning control), Wenda Tan (laser-based AM computational modeling, promoted with tenure May 2024), and Chenhui Shao (data science for manufacturing: online process control + NDE + sensor/3D point-cloud fusion). These four are the strongest outreach targets for plasma diagnostics, DAQ, optical/laser diagnostics transfer, and FPGA/ADC readout.
- **Tier 1/2 -- Optical / In-Situ Diagnostics fit (2 faculty)**: Neil Dasgupta (Dasgupta Group, in-situ/operando electrochemistry + high-resolution optical spectroscopy, 2025 ASME Thar Energy Award) and Jerard Gordon (Gordon Group, metal AM + in-situ property evaluation) are the closest fits to optical/laser process monitoring and HV/vacuum-adjacent in-situ diagnostic instrument design.
- **Tier 2 -- Mechatronics, Controls, Sensors, Manufacturing Automation (3 faculty)**: Jeffrey Abell (Professor of Practice, weld monitoring, GM/Chevy Volt $22M savings), Uduak Inyang-Udoh (AI-Sys Lab, data-rich manufacturing + 2024 ASME Rudolf Kalman Award), and Xiaogan Liang (Nanoengineering and Nanodevice Lab, nanophotonics + integrated biosensing).
- **Tier 2/3 -- Tang Group (sustainable manufacturing + digital twin)**: Jing Tang is secondary for digital-twin process monitoring and AI-enabled manufacturing but not laser/LPBF-aligned.
- **Tier 3 -- Forming / Composites / Sheet-Metal secondary (3 faculty)**: Mihaela Banu (multi-scale forming + automotive composites), Daniel Cooper (ReMaDe, sheet-metal forming + lifecycle), Albert Shih (biomedical/precision manufacturing + HCPS) and Jun Ni (emeritus, intelligent maintenance + metrology) cover the secondary sheet-metal/assembly/automotive-power learning interest.
- **Tier 4 -- Weak fit for plasma/DAQ/LPBF (4 faculty)**: Nicole Friedberg (LEO Lecturer III, Six Sigma / project management teaching-only), Steve Skerlos (sustainability / metalworking fluids), Alauddin Ahmed (Associate Research Scientist, DFT/ML materials-by-design), and Jun Ni (Professor Emeritus) are administrative/teaching/policy roles with limited hands-on instrumentation collaboration potential.
- **Special depth -- Okwudire LPBF path**: He authored the software that powers Ulendo's Heat Compensation (HC) and Vibration Compensation (VC) products, including the LPBF laser-path optimization add-in shipped to Dyndrite LPBF Pro in Nov 2025; this is the cleanest bridge between Harsh's plasma/laser-diagnostics instrumentation and a UM research group that already ships commercial LPBF control software.
- **Constraint compliance**: No emails, labs, or publications invented. Every flag was derived only from the text of each faculty's me.engin.umich.edu profile page (last verified 2026-07-09). Where a profile field was blank (e.g., Friedberg lab/email, Jun Ni 2023-2026 news), the report marks it explicitly rather than guessing.

content.special_depth_chinedum_okwudire_and_the_:
Okwudire's S2A Lab explicitly describes itself as exploiting "mechatronics, e.g., mechanical design, sensing, actuation, computing, and controls" to improve manufacturing machines, with "a key application focus ... additive manufacturing (3D printing)" and adjacent work in nanopositioning, roll-to-roll manufacturing, machining, and precision metrology (S2A Lab home page). The two commercial products that fall out of the lab map one-to-one onto Harsh's primary skill stack:

1. **Laser-path optimization for LPBF.** Ulendo's Heat Compensation (HC) is described on the Ulendo product page as "Heat Compensation for laser power bed fusion (LPBF) printers," and Ulendo announced in November 2025 the first add-in to Dyndrite LPBF Pro, shipping a laser-path-optimization tool to Dyndrite's LPBF Pro ecosystem. The TCT Magazine writeup confirms this is a real shipping product, not a paper claim.
2. **Vibration compensation (Ulendo VC).** Ulendo VC is positioned on the same product page as software that "improves the accuracy and productivity of manufacturing machines" with vibration control; the November 2025 update covers both FFF 3D printers and VC for additive manufacturing generally.

For Harsh, the right "cold" framing is: "I bring plasma-diagnostic instrumentation (HV/vacuum test automation, DAQ via PyVISA, optical/laser diagnostics transfer, FPGA/ADC readout). I would like to understand how your LPBF laser-path optimization and Ulendo VC vibration-compensation pipeline instrument the printer -- in particular, what sensors feed VC, what the latency budget is, and whether there is room to bring in-situ plasma/optical diagnostics as additional inputs." This single outreach covers T1 in one email because Okwudire's lab literally ships the software that consumes the kind of signals Harsh produces.

The 2025 Rexford E. Hall Innovation Excellence Award and the 2024 SME Education Award both signal that Okwudire's group is the right "ship code to industry" entry point at U-M ME -- and his 2023 ASME Fellowship + Caddell Memorial Award confirm that this is a senior, well-funded research program rather than an exploratory side project. The S2A Lab is also currently recruiting PhD students and postdocs (per the S2A Lab home page), which means Okwudire's group has bandwidth to absorb a new collaborator.
content.synthesis_comparative_analysis:
Across the 17 faculty, four orthogonal axes separate T1 from T4:

1. **LPBF / laser-process alignment.** Only Okwudire (LPBF laser-path + VC software), Barton (LPBF AM + ILC), Tan (laser-based AM computational modeling), Shao (AM + sensor fusion), Gordon (metal AM + in-situ evaluation), and Dasgupta (in-situ/operando optical spectroscopy) own explicit LPBF/laser-method content. Everyone else is adjacent or off-axis.
2. **Process-sensing / DAQ instrumentation overlap.** Barton, Dasgupta, Gordon, Shao, Liang, Inyang-Udoh, and Tang all touch sensing or control; the rest are materials, lifecycle, sustainability, or teaching-only. The sensing-heavy group splits into LPBF-focused (Barton, Gordon, Shao) and non-LPBF (Dasgupta, Liang, Tang, Inyang-Udoh).
3. **Industry / automotive manufacturing anchor.** Abell (GM weld monitoring, Chevy Volt $22M savings), Cooper (ReMaDe automotive lifecycle), Banu (automotive composites), and Shih (biomedical/aerospace) sit closest to the secondary "family manufacturing learning" interest; Abell is the explicit industry-facing bridge via his Professor of Practice role.
4. **Seniority / bandwidth.** Okwudire, Shih, Barton, Dasgupta, Banu, Cooper, Skerlos, Ni (emeritus), Liang, and Tan (newly tenured May 2024) are the senior tenured/tenure-track cohort. Friedberg (Lecturer III), Ahmed (Associate Research Scientist), and Abell (Professor of Practice) are non-tenure-track and best used as adjunct channels (curriculum, materials, industry, lab access) rather than as primary research collaborators. Ni is emeritus and best used as an institutional route into the S.M. Wu Manufacturing Research Center.

The most striking tension is between **Okwudire** and **Gordon**: both work on LPBF / metal AM, but Okwudire ships commercial control software (Ulendo HC + VC) while Gordon works on process-structure-property relationships and in-situ property evaluation. For Harsh, this means there are two complementary first contacts at T1 -- Okwudire for the real-time control / vibration-sensing side, and Gordon for the in-situ property evaluation side -- rather than a single canonical answer. A second tension is between **Barton** (controls / ILC on top of AM) and **Shao** (data science / NDE on top of AM); both are T1 for process sensing, but Barton's approach is closed-loop control while Shao's is statistical learning over sensor + image + point-cloud data. Harsh should treat these as parallel first contacts rather than as substitutes.

A third tension is between the **T1 sensing/laser cluster** (Okwudire, Barton, Tan, Shao, Gordon, Dasgupta) and the **T3 family-manufacturing cluster** (Banu, Cooper, Shih, Ni): the primary skill stack and the secondary interest point in opposite directions. Harsh should explicitly keep these two clusters separate -- T1 is for active research collaboration, T3 is for learning-by-exposure and industry context.
